hook: If you've been told you're "too much" enough times that you now shrink yourself before anyone can say it — you need to hear what actually happened there.
body:
**If you've been told you're "too much" enough times — too intense, too loud, too emotional, too much — you didn't just hear feedback. You received an instruction.**

And you followed it.

You learned to arrive already edited. To turn the volume down before anyone complained. To make yourself smaller as a pre-emptive act of protection.

The thing is, that strategy worked. People stopped saying it. The discomfort went away. So your nervous system filed it away as: this is how to be safe in rooms.

But here's what it cost you.

The qualities that got labelled "too much" — your intensity, your emotional depth, your full engagement — those are not your flaws. They are the exact qualities that, when expressed in the right context, are the most connecting thing about you.

You didn't become less charismatic. You became less visible.

And the people who made you feel like too much — they were not a reliable measure of your value. They were a measure of their own discomfort with someone who felt things fully.

The work now isn't about becoming louder. It's about selectively choosing where it's safe to take up your full space again.

More on this in my bio.
